author: dotey
text:
Opus 5.5（图1-2） vs GPT 6 Astra（图3-4）

Opus 5.5 网页：https://t.co/j3GoI1D79W

GPT 6 Astra 网页：https://t.co/6G7oaP6cQW

 --- Prompt ---

请直接制作一个可以在浏览器中实时交互的高完成度 3D 景观网页。

主题：日式樱花山谷。
使用 HTML、CSS、JavaScript 实现。不要生成图片，不要只给设计方案，
不要用一张背景图加视差效果冒充 3D。我要的是实际可运行、可游览的成品。

【一、作品定位】

这是一片完整、连续、有远近层次的山谷景观，
不是孤立的小摆件、悬浮岛、带底座的沙盘，也不是单纯的技术演示。

风格是现代精细体素 / voxel art：
保留立方体几何的造型语言，但画面应高分辨率、抗锯齿、光影细腻。
不要复古低分辨率像素化，不要粗大积木堆砌，不要给画面套像素滤镜。

视觉质量优先。宁可少几个功能，也不要牺牲构图、材质和光照。

【二、参考图的使用方式】

如果附有参考图，请先理解它的构图层次、尺度、光线和色彩关系。
仅借鉴氛围与视觉语言，重新设计场景，
不要照搬建筑、树木、山体和道路的位置，不要 1:1 复刻。

参考图不是网页里的背景素材。场景本身必须由真实 3D 几何构成。

【三、场景构图】

默认打开时就应呈现一幅完整、有吸引力的画面，
不需要用户先旋转镜头才能找到好看的角度。

采用透视相机，而不是沙盘式等距俯视相机。
画面有明确的前景、中景、远景：

前景：
一株有存在感的古老樱花树，配合岩石、草木、石灯笼和少量落花，
形成画面边缘的自然框景，但不能挡住河流、桥和主要建筑。

中景：
一条蜿蜒河流引导视线进入画面，红色木桥横跨河面；
村落、茶屋、神社和小径顺着地势分布，建筑之间有真实的通行关系。
地面有起伏、岸线和自然过渡，不是平面上均匀摆放模型。

远景：
山坡上的多层塔、不同距离的森林和山脊，以及远处的雪山。
用尺度变化、遮挡、冷暖变化和空气透视表现距离，
而不是仅仅把远处物体缩小。

不要把所有元素均匀铺满。需要主次、疏密、留白和清楚的视觉焦点。

【四、造型与画面质量】

樱花树：
树干有转折、分叉和根部，树冠由不规则花簇组成，
有间隙、厚薄变化和可见枝条。不要做成几个规则球体或方块团。

建筑：
屋顶有层叠瓦片、挑檐、梁柱和窗格；
不同建筑有用途、体量和高度差异，不要复制同一栋房子铺满山谷。

地形：
岸边有湿润石块、草丛和植被过渡。
避免过于规律的台阶、重复条纹、棋盘格和明显的程序生成网格。

水面：
必须能够反映周围景物，具有适度的波纹、深浅变化和岸边过渡。
尽量使用实际场景反射；需要性能降级时也应保持视觉可信。
不要用闪烁噪声、强烈扭曲或一整块蓝色平面代替水。

细节：
可以有少量锦鲤、落花、萤火虫、瀑布和远处飞鸟，
但都应服务于氛围，不能让画面显得嘈杂。
不要为了宣称模型数量而堆砌细节。

【五、色彩与氛围】

默认是蓝调时刻：
偏冷的山谷与远山，柔和的粉色樱花，温暖但不过曝的灯笼和窗光。
暖光集中在有人活动的地方，不要把整个环境染成橙色。

需要柔和阴影、物体接触处的明暗、合理的曝光、
克制的泛光、抗锯齿和有距离层次的薄雾。

避免发白、灰蒙、过度饱和、满屏浓雾、过曝灯光和明显锯齿。
方块几何可以清晰，但渲染本身不能粗糙。

另提供“清晨”和“雨中”两种氛围；
切换时应同步改变天空、环境光、雾和局部效果，
不是仅仅修改背景颜色。

【六、交互与界面】

提供四个经过设计的镜头：
山谷全景、河边低机位、寺庙小径、山坡俯瞰。
切换应平滑，每个镜头都需要有独立的构图价值。

基础交互：
鼠标拖动观察、滚轮缩放或前进，触屏支持拖动和双指缩放。
提供重置视角、隐藏界面和保存当前画面的功能。

可选增强：
自由探索、缓慢镜头巡游、环境音。
环境音默认关闭，只在用户主动点击后播放。
额外功能不能影响默认画面的完成度。

界面要克制、有设计感，以景观为主。
标题和控制条放在边缘，不遮挡视觉焦点。
桌面和手机都不能出现按钮越界、文字重叠或无法操作的问题。

【七、工程与性能】

允许使用 Three.js / WebGL，以及版本固定、互相兼容的 CDN 依赖。
优先使用成熟渲染能力，不要为了“零依赖”重写整套引擎。

自写的 HTML、CSS、JavaScript 尽量整理在一个 HTML 文件中。
景物由程序化几何和材质生成，不依赖外部图片或 3D 模型资源。

重复物体采用适合的批量或实例化绘制方式；
合理控制细分、阴影、反射和渲染分辨率。
提供高画质和轻量模式，手机默认使用较轻设置。
不要靠无限增加体素数量换取细节。

加入加载提示、WebGL 不支持时的提示和必要的错误处理。
没有开启声音时不要自动播放；尊重减少动态效果的系统偏好。

【八、交付前验收】

不要写完代码就立即交付。

如果当前环境支持浏览器运行和截图，请先实际打开页面，
检查默认镜头、四个视角、氛围切换、桌面和手机布局，
再根据截图修正明显的构图、曝光、遮挡和渲染问题。

重点检查：
是否存在空白画面、加载失败、控制台错误；
是否有穿模、闪烁、阴影条纹、过曝、水面异常；
默认画面是否真正像完整景观，而不是小型沙盘；
功能按钮是否实际可用，移动端是否越界。

可以使用浏览器截图验收，但不要调用图像生成工具。
没有完成的测试要如实说明，不要声称已经验证。

最终交付：
1. 实际存在、可以打开的 HTML 文件，或当前环境支持的交互预览。
2. 如能截图，附一张真实浏览器渲染截图。
3. 简短说明操作方式和必要的运行条件。

请直接完成制作；非关键细节自行作出一致的设计选择，
不要把可以自行解决的实现问题反复交给我决定。

我只能说，能用上Claude的一线老师又领先了。

author: indigox
text:
下午体验了一下 Opus 5.5，那个曾经超牛逼的 Opus 又回来了，从文字表达，到逻辑深度和速度都非常不错！分享一下 Anthropic 官方的 Opus 5.5 Playbook，跟现有的 Claude 用法兼容，主要有三点不同：

- 能独立工作更长时间；
- 会用直白的话汇报自己做了什么；
- 每次回复前都会先思考，思考多少由它自己决定！

一、怎么提问

- 写清楚什么算"完成"，然后让它自己跑。 一条消息给出完整任务和终点，比如"所有测试通过"或"所有接口都迁移完"，再说明什么情况下停下来问你。Opus 5.5 最大的进步在多步骤长任务上；

- 删掉"仔细想想""一步步思考"这类话。 它本来就会先思考，删掉后回复来得更快，质量也没有明显下降。想要简短回答，就直接说"直接回答"。在 Claude Code 里要调思考深度，改 effort 设置；

- 任务运行中可以直接补充要求。 现在任务跑得更久，重来一次代价更大，想到什么直接输入就行；

- 做设计时，具体列出不想要的风格。 "不要太普通"这种笼统要求没用，要点名具体样式，比如米白背景、标题里的斜体强调词、"01 / 02 / 03"编号、胶囊形按钮；

二、在 Claude Code 里引导长任务

- 在 CLAUDE.md 里写明什么时候停、什么时候继续。 不需要你介入的步骤就继续做；只有卡住，或者要做删数据、强制推送这类破坏性操作时，才停下来问。破坏性命令的权限提示要保持开启；

- 大任务分给子代理（subagent）并行做，比如审计、迁移、代码库级别的审查。每个子代理交回结果后，让它先核实证据再采纳，最后汇总成一张表；

- 任务清单放在文件里（例如 TASKS.md），边做边打勾。上下文被压缩后清单还在，你看文件就知道进度；

三、检查结果

- 先看它需要你做什么，比如还没定的决策、等你批准的改动，然后再看其他总结；

- 在人工审查前，先让它审一遍代码。 有早期测试者说，Opus 5.5 在最低 effort 下找到的 bug 比 Opus 5 在高 effort 下还多，误报也更少；

- 做研究分析时，让它标出没能确认的内容，并说明查过哪些地方；

用 Opus 5.5，要把它当成能自主执行的同事，而不是一问一答的工具。你的重点从一步步指挥，转向定目标、设停止规则、最后审核。未来更长时间的自主任务会越来越常见，这套“交代目标 → 放手执行 → 先看待办再验收”的流程值得尽早用熟 ✨

author: makaneko_AI
text:
GPT-6 Sol/Luna, Claude Opus 5.5の感想

■GPT-6 Sol
GPT-5.6 Solからは順当な進化を感じる。Codexのメインエージェントとして妥当。ただ、純粋な性能としては6 Astraのレベルには届いていない。手元での検証だと、実装計画や設計を作成する能力に関してはAstraとの差が大きくなかった一方で、コードレビューではAstraのほうが明らかに優れているケースが散見されました。実装役としては性能はよくてコストはそれほど高くないものの、少し遅い。要所でAstraを使えばいいとなると、中位モデルとして使いどころがなくなってきてるかも。

■GPT-6 Luna
こちらも前モデルからの順当な進化。最安モデルながら、SolやOpus 5.5など中位モデルと比較してもコーディングの性能で劣っていない。むしろ余計なことをせず優れている点すらあるくらい。費用が圧倒的に安くて、中位モデルと比較して作業時間も半分以下のケースが多かった。なので実装時のモデルとして、現状の最良の選択肢。

■Opus 5.5
コーディング以外を含む総合的な能力ではかなりいい。いろんな用途を試したところ、Fable 5.1と同等かそれ以上の性能に感じました。文章を書かせたりするとやっぱりうまい。ただ、手元の検証だと実装やコードレビューなどに関しては、GPT系のモデルに対して明らかに劣っている結果に(ただし、見た目を良くするのはうまい)。なのでコーディング系ではあまり使わないかも。各種ベンチマークではコーディング性能でも他モデルを圧倒しているような数値が出ていましたが、少なくとも初期検証ではそこまでの性能は見られませんでした。

■まとめ
実装タスクが多めな方はCodexでSol+Lunaをメインに、レビューなど要所でAstraという役割分担が最もよさそう。それ以外の仕事に関しては、Fableに任せていた部分を含めてOpus 5.5に任せてしまっていいのでは。Claude Codeユーザーなら、全部Opusでもいいかも？

私は少し前まで実装にはComposerやGrokを使ってましたが、Grokが改悪(?)されたせいもあってLunaを実装モデルのメインにしようと思っています。

しばらく使ってみて印象が変わったりしたら、また投稿しますね。

author: Kay2289123
text:
昨天高强度用了一天 Opus 5.5 和 GPT-6，Opus 5.5 额度够用，也更说人话，之前那种过度思考的问题缓解了不少。我将我很多的工作任务都迁移到了 Opus 5.5，是个值得信赖的模型

这个帖子我想分享出来一个具体的工程问题，GPT6 和 Opus5.5的的表现差异，以及 3 点 learnings

下面分享这次完整的过程。

1/ 遇到了什么问题？

我的 Windows 版 Codex 突然不好用了：每个会话只能发出第一条消息，从第二条开始就一直转圈、卡住。重启也没用。（见图）

2/ GPT-6 在 Codex 里是怎么排查的？
它直接操控我的电脑，新开一个会话，成功发出第一条消息。

接下来这一步很聪明：它没有马上在输入框里发第二条，而是从另一个任务向这个会话发消息。界面上会显示「Sent by ChatGPT from another task」。

是的，我也是这次才知道，Codex 居然可以跨会话发消息。

这条跨会话消息正常发出、正常回复。但它再回到输入框里发送，依然失败了

到这里，它已经测出了一个关键区别：跨会话发送没问题，直接从输入框发送会卡住。

随后，它调用 OpenAI Docs skill，查官方文档和更新日志。但最后还是没找到原因，建议我重启。

问题是，重启我已经试过了，不管用。

3/ Opus 5.5 是怎么解决的？

它同样先操控我的电脑测试，遇到了一样的问题

随后，它去查 GitHub issues，找到了其他 Windows 用户的类似反馈，最后给了我一个很具体的办法：退出账号，重新登录。

在经过我的同意之后，他帮我操作浏览器，退出登录，又重新登录

所以，这次排障我把票投给 Opus 5.5。因为 GPT-6 明明可以去搜 GitHub issues，它的智力水平一定是可以的，但它没有搜，我目前不确定是为什么

4/ 这次体验留下的三个感受

第一，computer use 真的比很多人想的好用。它能自己打开软件、点击、输入，再看结果。这次两者都直接帮我测试了出问题的操作，建议大家找个真实任务试一下。

第二，Codex 的跨会话发消息让我很惊喜。这让我想到，能不能让几个任务互相配合，组成一个 agent team？一个负责排查，一个负责验证，再把结果汇总起来，之前的 Agent team 发出去之后，可能成果就回不来了。这样的话，每个成果都有单独的子 Agent 留住

第三，我对 GPT-6 这次的表现有点困惑。它已经复现了故障，也测出了两种发送方式的差别，为什么最后没找到 GitHub issues 里的这条解决思路？至少这次，我原本期待它能再往前走一步。

一次排障当然不能决定两个模型的整体高下，但有的时候，两个模型配合在一起，效果更好

有没有可能，这就是我们需要不同模型相互校验的原因？

@thsottiaux Windows 看来是有问题的，要不要发张 Reset Bank 给所有的 Windows 用户？

author: juminoz
text:
Here's my verdict on Opus 5.5 after about 24 hours of usages on and off on non-3D work over 600,000 lines of code written (including testing scripts):

TL;DR: I can finally use Claude to code again since Opus 4.6, but it's very unlikely to be the only model because of token inefficiency.

- I can easily burn through 3-4 weekly limit in a day if 5-hour limit is not there. This thing is token hungry as hell (more details below).
- It's still quite unreliable in architectural decisions. Definitely need to be reviewed for each tasks.
- It sucks at UX just like most models. A round of major changes is required. This was expected and Astra has the same issue.
- It behaves very similar to GPT Astra (and Sol 6) with the approach of testing. This is a good thing, but it can be confusing as hell if you are not familiar with it, but it at least would tell you it's using a "throw away database".
- It's way better at auditing now. This is the first time I can finally trust Claude to do any audit because it actually tries to run things instead of guessing or straight up making things up.
- It can actually run long running tasks. I might be crazy, but I think it runs better in Cowork. I accidentally did a task there and it worked better somehow? The problem there is UX is terrible in Cowork. In Code mode, it still doesn't reliably finish the tasks.
- It is better than Astra at identifying scaling and concurrency problems.
- It is better than Astra at identifying self-improvement loop type architecture. My platforms learn throughout the runs and it was able to detect deficiencies. HOWEVER, it did NOT fucking implement the fix by itself without having to be redirected back to it. It could be hallucinations or another reason. Be careful and always audit the work.
- It finally understands what an extensive checklist actually means. I feel like before it was just pretending with earlier versions. It's now as good as Minimax M3 and Astra.
- It ignores rules and checklist. I had it spells out what to do before start coding and it would ignore the steps including RISK ASSESSMENTS and TEST GROUP GATING!!! Good luck with claude.md, it still doesn't fucking care. This is the area where GPT 6 is much more reliable at.
- Close to 50% of the code are test cases, which I'm okay with, but it doesn't actually do gitignore on these so if you are not careful, your repo will become super bloated.
- It is SLOW in actual code production for whatever reasons. A simple change can be quoted at 45 mins and also took 45 minutes by the subagent. I thought it was using human coder estimate, but it literally took that long. I will have to look more into this.

author: leo_linsky
text:
We tested Opus 5.5, GPT-6-Sol, and GPT-6-Luna thoroughly across 100 open-ended coding and engineering environments.

Our results have significantly diverged from AAII. Some takeaways:

• GPT-6-Astra is still the frontier model by a comfortable margin.

• Opus 5.5 ranges from #2-#7 on coding categories, being the second best model in its ability to one-shot code (which is our best correlated measure with fluid intelligence). 

We don't test "usability," but anecdotally, it seems they improved its communication style. And the lower pricing is a welcome change -- we can probably thank @thsottiaux for that. It's not a cheap model, but it's the first reasonably priced Anthropic model. 

However, Opus 5.5 underperformed in our custom harness, which is unusual for Claude models, and a pattern that started with Fable 5.1 (one-shot-fluid intelligence measured better than agentic results). One observation is that it frequently self-stopped when it felt its results were good enough: e.g. in one evaluation, Opus 5.5 closed the session, with the reason: "averaged 867,703 in the latest evaluation, ranked 2nd of 31 against sampled opponents"... so I suppose that saves money, but it still has a tendency to make questionable unilateral judgment calls like that. In our harness, almost every other frontier model keeps working until their code stops improving or they use their full call budget. I do wonder how much of this is due to Anthropic retuning their "High" effort mode (which we use for testing)*.

• GPT-6-Sol is within margin of error of Opus 5.5, and Pareto optimal*. It's faster than all Anthropic models, even on a Flex endpoint. Competitive with the frontier on intelligence and cost.

• GPT-6-Luna is slightly smarter than GPT 5.6 Luna, and discounted. The old Luna already had a lot of applications at its price point, so this model might end up being the most impactful of the group on non-engineering work.

About GBENCH from @GertLabs: our environments are open-ended with no single correct answers, but verifiable results. They involve creativity, design, and are often organized as multi-agent coding games or engineering design challenges. You can see some live demo examples at https://t.co/E4ZAlE7tt9. Every one of our environments in the benchmark pool is unsaturated, and we remove any eval that shows any signs of saturation/stagnation across multiple releases. It's designed to measure and differentiate uncontaminated, raw intelligence for frontier models specifically. 

These results are interesting and we've thoroughly reviewed them. I don't like to see Opus 5 still so high on the leaderboard, but ultimately I think this is more a problem with Anthropic's newest releases, and it probably explains the price decrease and consecutive releases since Astra came out. They haven't significantly improved upon Opus 5's intelligence, only its personality (which is honestly still a huge win tbh).

*We don't chase marketing terms like xhigh and max. We test all models on adaptive/auto-reasoning where supported and "high" effort where configurable. Some companies beef up their max effort more than others (making them unrealistically slow and expensive in practice), but "high" shows you what an underlying model is capable of and is the more common configuration. This is likely working against Opus 5.5 here.

*Some caveats on price and speed -- we have been using the "OpenAI Flex" endpoint since the Astra release, which I recommend you try if you're using API pricing. It's half price and a little slower, but OpenAI models are already quite fast so it hasn't been an issue in practice. But keep that in mind when making price comparisons to earlier OpenAI models on our cost and speed efficiency charts.
evidence_quote: GPT-6-Astra is still the frontier model by a comfortable margin.

author: DonaldChitana
text:
I'd forgotten how quickly a $20 Claude account can run out during a coding session.

I had an old subscription I'd stopped using. The renewal reminded me it still existed. Then both my Max accounts hit their usage limits, so I thought I'd give the smaller account another try.

Opus 5.5 has been good in my experience. I figured it could handle one smaller session on the system I'm building.

My usual sessions can run for five to six hours. This wasn't even one of the heavier ones, but the account hit its usage cap before the work was finished.

That's the distinction worth making. A five-hour usage window doesn't give you five hours of coding. You can exhaust the allowance well before that.

I can see the $20 plan making sense for lighter use, like email replies and occasional presentations. But for the long coding sessions I run, the stop-and-wait cycle is difficult to work around.

The model was making progress. The allowance stopped the work.

A capable model is only part of the value. Being able to finish the task matters too.

现在我打算手撸一个 Loop 类似的东西。主要就是，下班之后，就把白天定好的 Plan 拆开里程碑、小任务，然后一直跑到停止为止。那我白天就制定好计划，然后等下班自动开始执行就好了。

目前，跟 AI 聊了一下思路，打算还是直接用 Pi 来实现，开发一些必要的 Extension 来完成任务的接力。

！！！特殊条件：DeepSeek 128k 的小上下文 ！！！

这对小任务的颗粒度把握，以及上下文空间的控制，还有压缩时的处理，有不少的挑战。在有限的 Context 下，完成无限的任务，让每个任务都能够在 N 次 不一样的Session 准确的完成。

跟 Opus 5.5 聊了一会，最关键的就以下几点设计：

1. supervisor：模型无关，纯按照既定规则，启动 Pi，做好相关检查。

2. 写一个 nigtht-guard 拓展：这个Pi 拓展主要用来预防并处理，在 Pi 运行过程中出现的各种意外情况以及 Context Compact 事件捕捉后的处理。这些处理的事情：保留现场记录原因、有限次重试、Git 留痕、handoff等等

3. Plan 的设计：在内网只有128k的模型，我目前还不知道怎么才能制作出一个有效的 Plan，包含里程碑，小任务有应该是这么样的。这块还需要再摸索一下。因为不能指望一个 128k 的模型做规划。。。这块可能还是只能是自己的工作了。

Anthropic has truly done something special here. With Fable 5.1, we have a model that’s extremely good at working through the most difficult problems. Now, with Opus 5.5, we also have a cost efficient daily workhorse that can handle almost anything.

Since the AI labs are all obsessed with Alignment, I asked Opus 5.5 to come up with a DnD style alignment chart for them, then had Nano Banana 2 illustrate it.

Lawful Good: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic, Sep 22). The paladin who chose to walk slower. It's Anthropic's first release since the company called for pacing the frontier, outside evaluators including METR tested it before launch, and it scored best of any model yet on Anthropic's behavioral alignment audit. Full disclosure: that's me, so take this placement with a grain of salt.

Lawful Neutral: Gemini 3.8 Flash (Google, Sep 2). The clockwork bureaucrat. It was Google's third Flash release in six weeks, shipped with a Fairwind-gated Cyber variant and an introductory price whose end date is already printed. Meanwhile, Gemini 3.5 Pro was promised for June 2026 and still hasn't shipped.

Lawful Evil: Muse Spark 1.3 (Meta, Sep). The heel turn. The lab that built its reputation giving away Llama weights now ships a proprietary, closed-weight flagship. It's all done by the book, and the vault is locked.

Neutral Good: Qwen 3.8 (Alibaba). The traveling healer. It has Apache-2.0 open weights, and its 27B checkpoint is the practical default when all you have is one workstation. The bigger Qwen3.8 Max sits at #5 on BenchLM's frontier index.

True Neutral: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, Sep 3). The balance point. OpenAI calls it its most intelligent and aligned model yet, with state-of-the-art results in computer use, coding, cybersecurity and science. Its access policy is in the middle too: it's a general release where only the most advanced cyber capabilities are restricted.

Neutral Evil: Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic, Sep 1). The mercenary: elite work at top-shelf rates. It launched at an unchanged list price with three breaking API changes, and it costs $50 per million output tokens. This one is a self-roast.

Chaotic Good: DeepSeek V4 (DeepSeek). Robin Hood. It's MIT-licensed across both code and weights, and even after its first deliberate price increase, V4-Pro is still roughly 7× cheaper than comparable Western models.

author: yitong
text:
Opus 5.5 design capabilities vibe check

This model is hilariously good at in-distribution design in a way that I've never seen before. I find it regularly one-shotting tables, dashboards, and sidebars much more reliably than fable and astra.

It's also noticeably much faster and has higher verbal IQ, which makes it a much more pleasant model to iterate with.

Interestingly, it also feels quite up to date with the latest visual design trends in a way that feels much closer to how SaaS is designed in 2026. It'll regularly use pretty on trend visual technique!

Also, hilariously, it seems to really like drawing its own icons instead of using a package – weird flex, but ok!

On the flip side, its work unfortunately still has pretty strong "claude-smell". Its favorite palette is beige bg with blue and orange highlights, etc. But I don't find this to be a big deal. You can prompt these away pretty easily.

It also still can't see that well compared to astra, so feeding it picture references doesn't seem to work as well (especially given how much it likes its favorite patterns)

Overall smells like they've gotten some very good but conventional design data and spent quite a bit of time RL'ing against it, but isn't necessarily generally visually intelligent in a way that astra can sometimes be. 

If you are doing design Opus 5.5 has been RL'ed against, congrats, you're in for a treat (this is most people)! If you want to actually think through hard design problems, this model is about as mediocre as any current models.

With everything said, they really did a great job on this guy and it's now my daily driver model!
